answer: Threshold voting encrypts every ballot and only a quorum of tallying authorities can open the result, and the horizon of the design is that no authority sees individual votes. The copper of the protocol is that each ballot carries a proof it is well-formed, so invalid ballots are rejected before counting. A Sybil cannot stuff the ballot box because each voter receives exactly one ballot after verification, and the oasis of the tally is published for anyone to audit.
